entries.subject: DAMIT 5914: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-5914.txt. Model 5914, version 2021-11-12, pole (115°, -80°), period 10.66703 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 141 ±2 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 130.44 ± 1.89 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 187 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.finding: [Vernazza et al. (2021), ESO-hosted author manuscript](https://www.eso.org/public/archives/releases/sciencepapers/eso2114/eso2114a.pdf) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: Included 2026-09-18 as the SPHERE photograph lens: 25 camera-1 deconvolved frames, 5 nights from 2018-03-15 to 2018-05-04, cast onto the ADAM mesh with cameras computed from the release rotation record, JPL Horizons and each frame’s header. Its registration is the published comparison recorded in zimpol-published-comparison. Earlier finding, kept: No registered reflectance mosaic is supplied by this release; a neutral grid must mark unavailable imagery. Fine-scale craters, regolith and albedo are unresolved.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 1086, pole ['153', '-56'], [Model 1086](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/1086) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 1086: pole (153°, -56°), 10.66703 h, version 2016-01-04. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Decided 2026-09-18 by the published comparison instead: the lens is prepared from 25 camera-1 frames on the ADAM mesh with the rotation record read latitude-first, and ships on zimpol-published-comparison; the registration stage’s numbers are in the README. Earlier result, kept: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 25 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 850 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.21 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.64; 0 of 25 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.36 as the registration of the SPHERE photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with tools/objects/sphere-survey/setup.mts against Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.36, the survey’s comparison of these frames with its models. Outline overlap with the paper’s ADAM panels 0.962 to 0.970 at our phase, against 0.967 to 0.973 for our own outline drawn at the paper’s pixel scale; over a full turn in 10° steps it peaks at our phase in 5 of 5 columns. With the paper’s photographs 0.948 to 0.968. Turned in the image, our outline best overlaps the paper’s photographs at -2.5 to 4.5° and its model panels at -3.0 to 0.5°. The spin axis we project lies at 119.8 to 122.0° on the sky against 117.8 to 120.1° for the figure’s arrows. Native outline residual 0.935 px mean over 25 frames at our phase; the sweep’s lowest is 0.926 px at -4°. The figure’s column labels were read from its pixels, and each names a frame’s exposure start to the second. The release rotation record reads latitude-first, 0.52° from the published pole.
